shortlist.label: Drug-induced psoriasiform eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is taking duvelisib, a PI3K inhibitor, which is known to cause psoriasiform skin reactions

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsies showed parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils, consistent with psoriasiform dermatitis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques and scaly papules, similar to pityriasis rubra pilaris

shortlist.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of follicular lymphoma and is taking medications that may contribute to seborrheic dermatitis

shortlist.label: Graft-versus-host disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lymphoma and is taking immunosuppressive medications, which may increase the risk of graft-versus-host disease

raw.rationale: The patient's skin eruption began after starting new medications, including duvelisib, and skin biopsies showed findings consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction, such as parakeratosis and dermal eosinophils.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy findings are similar to psoriasis, the subacute onset and temporal relationship with new medication use suggest a drug-induced reaction rather than a primary psoriatic process.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match the characteristic orange-red palmoplantar keratoderma and follicular hyperkeratosis of pityriasis rubra pilaris.

rejected.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
rejected.why: The distribution of the eruption and biopsy findings are not typical of seborrheic dermatitis, which usually involves the scalp, face, and central chest.

rejected.label: Graft-versus-host disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of a recent transplant or other risk factors for graft-versus-host disease, making this diagnosis unlikely.
